subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: What public policy boundary should ClawHub use for SKILL.md/README instructions that direct an agent to fetch code, change privileges, bypass confirmation, or act beyond the skill's stated purpose?
rationale: The repository has internal scanner guidance and adjacent unsafe-execution policy, but this RFC asks maintainers to set a marketplace acceptability boundary with security and publisher consequences.

options.title: Adopt an explicit guideline
options.body: Define acceptable, needs-review, and not-allowed agent-directed instruction classes, then document them in specs and public policy docs.

options.title: Tie the guideline to the capability manifest
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2944 so borderline instructions are judged against declared capabilities.

options.title: Keep this scanner-only
options.body: Do not add publisher-facing policy yet and leave these cases to ClawScan plus manual moderator review.

recommendation.title: Adopt an explicit guideline
recommendation.body: Define acceptable, needs-review, and not-allowed agent-directed instruction classes, then document them in specs and public policy docs.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and blame both point to this handle for the adjacent security docs and ClawScan policy surface.
